title: Obliviousness of the schedule
statement: For every finite Turing machine $W$ over the Boolean alphabet and every $a\in\mathbb{N}$, the schedule machine determined by $W$ and $a$ is oblivious: for any two inputs over its schedule alphabet of equal length and every time $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the input-head positions agree, and the entire tuples of work-tape head positions agree.
hypotheses_covered: W is a finite machine over Booleans
The two schedule-alphabet inputs have equal length
replaced:
For every clock witness $W$ over the Boolean alphabet and every parameter
$a \in \mathbb{N}$, the length-only schedule built from $W$ and $a$ is oblivious: on
arbitrary equal-length inputs over the schedule alphabet, its input head and every
clock, budget, counter, and guide head occupy the same position at every time. No
computation or halting hypothesis is needed.
